definition: Fatalistic means convinced that events are decided by fate and cannot be changed.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word fatalistic. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know fatalistic should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: Dario was fatalistic about auditions: 'They cast the part before you walk in,' he would shrug, 'so you might as well walk in relaxed.'
Passive people simply don't act — a milder condition than fatalistic, which supplies the reason no one should bother: the outcome is already written.
Nihilistic goes further than fatalistic: fatalism says the ending is fixed, nihilism says there was never any meaning in the story at all.

A defeatist is braced to lose this particular fight — the match, the election, the audit — and behaves as if the loss has already happened. Fatalistic runs wider and deeper: it says every outcome, wins included, was scripted in advance. A defeatist expects to lose; a fatalistic person expects nothing anyone does to matter.

Hopeless means without hope of any good outcome — the future looks dark from every angle. Fatalistic is not about darkness but about authorship: a fatalistic person may cheerfully expect good things, believing only that fate, never effort, will deliver them. Hopeless despairs of the ending; fatalistic just hands over the steering wheel.
